# Event-driven order fulfillment

Our commerce platform accepts an order through an API gateway and order service. The order service validates the request, assigns an order id and idempotency key, stores the pending order, and writes an OrderPlaced event to an outbox in the same database transaction. An outbox relay publishes events to the durable event bus, where consumers may receive duplicates and must record their processed event ids.

The payment consumer authorizes funds through the payment provider and emits either PaymentAuthorized or PaymentFailed. The inventory consumer reserves stock in the inventory database and emits InventoryReserved or InventoryUnavailable. A fraud consumer evaluates the order and emits FraudCleared or FraudRejected. An order coordinator waits for successful payment, inventory, and fraud results before emitting OrderConfirmed. A failure from any branch cancels the order and starts compensation for branches that already succeeded: payment authorization is voided and inventory is released.

Confirmed orders go to the fulfillment consumer, which creates warehouse work and later emits Packed. The shipping consumer buys a label from the carrier, records tracking, and emits Shipped. A notification consumer sends customer updates for confirmation, cancellation, and shipment. A read-model projector builds the customer order timeline used by the query API.

Each consumer has an idempotency store, bounded retries, and a dead-letter queue. Operators can repair and replay dead-lettered events while preserving the original event id and causation chain. The coordinator uses timeouts to cancel orders that never receive all required results, and late success events must run the appropriate compensation rather than reopening a terminal order. Correlation ids, traces, consumer lag, retry counts, and compensation outcomes feed the observability platform.
